findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. The 'what' and 'why' are answered before any detail about firstmate.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page says plainly why a study of another project (firstmate) sits on Athena's site. Without this, a newcomer would wonder why most of the page is about something other than Athena.
findings.source: Header lede: "A study is Athena's written reading of another software project... Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project"

findings.text: Next steps gives the requirements, a clone command, an install command and a first command to try, and the header links straight to them. One gap: it doesn't say which repository the request runs on, or whether running it needs an account or costs money.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" / "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: This link speaks to 'you' as if the reader were the owner. A newcomer can't tell whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Some definitions are circular or vague. 'Wake' is never defined, and the definition of 'ship' doesn't say what a ship is for. A newcomer can't build a clear picture from them.
findings.source: Glossary entries "stale wake" ("A wake after which the agent inspects a worker...") and "ship" ("A kind of task, named next to scouts")

findings.text: Several firstmate-internal terms appear in transition cards and claims without a glossary entry, so the deeper sections are hard to follow without reading firstmate itself.
findings.source: Transition t8 and claim c41: "re-reads its pin", "durable harness pin", "standing charter", "crewmates"; claim c37: "main first mate"

findings.text: The same facts are repeated many times, which makes the page long and hides the overview. Phrasing like 'The cited text states no...' adds to the dense, mechanical feel.
findings.source: "Words used first" and Glossary both define yolo, green, red, in scope; the yolo/red rule recurs under "What firstmate is", "One piece of work", "When things go wrong", t4, t10

findings.text: The state list shows only a name and a tag for each state. The useful meaning sits in the lead-in paragraph and the glossary, so the list on its own tells the reader little.
findings.source: States of a piece of work: "queued initial [c1] [c2] [c43]"
